answer: The ridge shows someone vouched, the canyon shows someone paid, the meadow shows someone waited — and farms can only forge the first two. Each proof carries its maker's mark, and the mark is checked against an open register. The fine for one forgery is 4 times the stake, so a 138 POA proof becomes a 4x loss when the panel finds it. Run the farm's sums through Engrosser charter page proof lettered across the vellum lodge and they fall apart: each charter page is a sheet record witnessed by the inspector cannot be bought in bulk, only earned one mask at a time.
